feedback: Approving the kp 3.5 to 3.0 step on the iteration 7 design. The candidate changes only controller.kp. Geometry (sensors at y = 0.07, x = -0.04 to +0.04, sensor_size 0.012), kd 0.8, base_speed 1.6, line_loss last_direction and sensor_weights are unchanged, so the race isolates the gain effect. Iteration 7 (kd 0.8, kp 3.5) is the best raced design at 304.77, with 13 of 20 oval finishes. Its s-bend and slalom runs still ended off track, with steering_oscillation of 0.23 and 0.25 and line_loss_events of 1.1 and 1.4. That is the over-steer signal the kp reduction targets. The candidate is inside the contract and is not obviously broken. I make no claim about how it will perform. Interpret the race as follows. If the score is at or above 304.77 and s-bend or slalom steering_oscillation falls toward 0.15 with progress above 0.30 and 0.19, keep kp 3.0. Next, try kp 2.5 with kd 0.8 kept. If oval finishes drop below iteration 7's 13 of 20, or the score falls below 304.77, kp 3.0 is too low for the oval. Return to kp 3.5 with kd 0.8. If the robot stays on track on all three tracks but misses the 3.0 s limit, then speed is the constraint, so raise base_speed toward 2.0. The oval mean finish of 1.90 s suggests speed is not the limit there, so do not raise it while the bends are still failing.
requested_changes: If the score is at or above 304.77 and s-bend or slalom steering_oscillation falls toward 0.15 with progress rising above 0.30 and 0.19: keep kd 0.8 and try controller.kp 2.5 to test whether further over-steer reduction holds the bends.

If oval finishes fall below iteration 7's 13 of 20, or the score drops below 304.77: return controller.kp to 3.5 with kd 0.8 kept, since the oval needs the stronger front-weighted steering that iteration 7 showed.

If the robot stays on track on all three tracks but misses the 3.0 s limit, raise controller.base_speed from 1.6 toward 2.0 with the chosen kp and kd, since oval mean finish time is 1.90 s and only the bends are failing.
